clue.text: 19 at sea in boats demonstrate enjoyment

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit within the word for boats, which is opened up to take them

parts.note: smacks are small sailing fishing boats

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters of the referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, the Greek letter epsilon

explanation.surface: Something about the number nineteen being out on the ocean in boats makes someone show pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges EPSILON (the answer to 19 down) into ONESLIP, and 'in' puts that inside SMACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Licking or smacking the mouth is a sign of relish, so the idiom means showing delight.

clue.text: Robin nested in these trees

parts.note: reads like a bird building a nest, but Robin is the outlaw Robin Hood, whose legendary home was a Nottinghamshire woodland

explanation.surface: A garden bird has made its nest in some woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: The robin looks like a bird; it is Robin Hood, who hid out in this forest in Nottinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places the outlaw Robin Hood and his band in this royal woodland near Nottingham.

clue.text: Harrow, where a European turns up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in northern Europe

explanation.surface: A question about Harrow, the school or town, where some European person appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses LAPPA (Lapp plus A) to give the answer. Harrow is a verb here: to distress, not the London school or the farm tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow someone is to distress or horrify them deeply, a synonym.

clue.text: Station put second in card vote

indicators.note: put in means the abbreviation for second is placed between the two words for card and vote

parts.note: a king is a court card in a pack
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: Someone at a station slots their card in second place in a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: KING'S CROSS is a major London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a major mainline railway terminus in north London.

clue.text: Offensive rumour about merit award

indicators.note: about means the rumour word goes around the award's letters

parts.note: noise can mean talk or rumour, as in noises about a takeover
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Unpleasant gossip is circulating about someone receiving an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OM (the Order of Merit, a British honour) inside NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisome is foul-smelling or objectionable, a synonym of offensive.

clue.text: Nurse is on the go early in the morning

indicators.note: being on the go means moving about busily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse is busy at work from dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the go' rearranges the letters of NURSE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, when the sun comes up, is the first part of the day.

clue.text: Press gives one man, …

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A newspaper gives one man some space, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 7 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them with a heated appliance, a synonym.

clue.text: Peter, on a drug trip, protection

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: a drug trip is a hallucinogenic experience, so the letters of a drug go wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: Peter, high on narcotics, is the guardian, continuing from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges A DRUG into GUARD. Peter is underworld slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A safeguard is a measure that protects against harm, a synonym.

clue.text: Sally has a wind instrument in a black box

parts.note: a sally is a sudden flight or sortie
the recorder is a woodwind instrument played in schools

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally keeps a woodwind instrument inside a dark case.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name; here it is a sortie or flight.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's data and voice logging device is popularly called the black box.

clue.text: Measure money paid and food provided

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure, half an em
a pension is a regular payment of money

explanation.surface: A gauge of payments received and meals laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: EN PENSION is French for boarding with meals included; an en is a printing measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying en pension means lodging with board included, so meals are part of the arrangement.

clue.text: Refuse to give ditch digger money

parts.note: King Offa of Mercia had Offa's Dyke, a great earthwork ditch, built along the Welsh border
L stands for the pound, librum, as in the sign for sterling

explanation.surface: Someone declines to pay a labourer who digs ditches.
explanation.walkthrough: The ditch digger is OFFA, the Anglo-Saxon king behind Offa's Dyke on the England-Wales border; L is the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal means waste matter or rubbish as well as entrails, so it is a synonym for refuse.

clue.text: City's water supply

explanation.surface: A town's source of drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells is a small cathedral city in Somerset, England; wells are holes sunk to draw water.

clue.text: Nameless Athenian about to pass over

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the shortened name is read backwards
nameless signals dropping the abbreviation for name, the letter N

parts.note: Timon of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: An anonymous citizen of Athens is about to ignore something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' removes N (name) from TIMON, leaving TIMO, and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or skip it is a synonym.

clue.text: Expecting a giant

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, as in Gog and Magog

explanation.surface: Awaiting a huge person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eagerly expectant or excited is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Just hurry — I am at the end of the line

parts.note: to leg it is slang for to run or hurry
I'm is the contraction

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: Rushing, someone gasps that they are at the last stop.
explanation.walkthrough: To leg it is British slang for running away. 'the end of' takes E from line.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and lawful are both senses of a valid, rightful claim.

clue.text: Main side has love song incorporating Beethoven's First

indicators.note: incorporating means the letter is taken into the body of the other pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a verse is a stanza of a song

indicators.note: the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A principal team has a romantic ballad that includes the opening of a Beethoven piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Main side means the principal face of a coin, not a top team; 'incorporating' puts B between O and VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the face of a coin or medal bearing the principal design.

clue.text: Destroy museum, uttering calumnies

parts.note: the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: uttering means the word for calumnies is spoken, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: calumnies are false statements, lies

explanation.surface: Someone smears a museum with slander to wreck it.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London. 'uttering' turns LIES into the sound-alike LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to deliberately damage or wreck, a synonym of destroy.

clue.text: Ingenious way to disguise a gentle

indicators.note: to disguise is to change appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever method for hiding a mild-mannered person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' rearranges A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegant solution is neat and clever, so it can mean ingenious.

clue.text: German city provided reciprocal art

indicators.note: reciprocal suggests going back the other way, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A city in Germany supplied art exchanged back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reciprocal' reverses ESSEN + IF as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is skill, delicacy or artfulness in handling something.

clue.text: Exotic character shows speech defect up in time

indicators.note: in means the reversed defect is placed inside the word for a long time

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a lisp is a speech impediment

explanation.surface: A strange person reveals a stammer that comes out in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LISP to PSIL, which 'in' puts inside EON. Exotic means foreign: a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign symbol to English readers.

clue.text: Note sieve used by cook

parts.note: G is a musical note
a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A memo about a strainer the chef uses.
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is a coarse garden sieve, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate a cook heats to fry on.

clue.text: The reason for Scottish policies

explanation.surface: Why the Scots adopted their political programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are the basis or motive for something; in Scots, policies are the parkland around a mansion.

clue.text: Ramble in, we hear, a city .

indicators.note: we hear means the letters entered sound like the word spoken

parts.note: Rome, the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Wander about in a city, they say, with the thought carried on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this to 22 across, whose definition shares 'a city'.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander aimlessly, a synonym of ramble.

clue.text: … in Czechoslovakia

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit within the country's name

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'a city' from 21 across, carried over by the dots; the letters are hidden in Czechoslovakia.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norwegian capital is a city, completing the shared clue.

clue.text: One said to stick round home

parts.note: Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: said means the letters entered sound like the word spoken

parts.note: glue means to stick

explanation.surface: Someone who is said to cling around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns GLUE into the sound-alike GLOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is domed and roughly circular, a round dwelling.

clue.text: Plenty see the notices

parts.note: lo means look or see
ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: A lot of people look at the advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is informal for a great deal, a lot.

clue.text: Hit for six — or seven

explanation.surface: A batsman strikes the ball over the boundary for six, maybe seven runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a small slam is a bid at the six level and a grand slam at seven; to hit for six is a cricket expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam means strike hard; in bridge, slams are contracts to win twelve or thirteen tricks, bids of six or seven.

clue.text: Just the same, good man and bad

parts.note: St is saint, a good man
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: Even so, decent and wicked people are alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means nevertheless, all the same.

clue.text: Chap had returned with help

parts.note: Len is a man's name

indicators.note: returned means the word had is read backwards

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: A man has come back with assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns HAD into DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: To help is to offer assistance, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Writer emends spurned characters in play

indicators.note: in play means put in motion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author revises characters that were rejected in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges the letters of EMENDS SPURNED; he wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: An Elizabethan poet, author of The Faerie Queene.
